heuristics: Before committing to a push intent, require that the player can reach the needed standing cell (the cell opposite the push direction from the box) in the *current* state; reject pushes whose standing cell is only reachable in the pre-push layout.

Treat 1-tile corridors and chokepoints as fragile: avoid pushing any box into a corridor if it reduces the player’s connectivity graph (creates a cut) unless that box is destined to stay there (goal or final storage).
Never push a box to a wall-adjacent cell if the only way to push it again would require standing in a corner/against a wall that will become inaccessible after the push (classic self-blocking).

Add a forward-check after each planned push: recompute reachable regions and ensure the next k planned pushes (at least the next 1–2) still have reachable standing cells; if not, backtrack immediately.
Avoid sequences that “staircase” a box back and forth (e.g., repeated Up/Down on the same column) unless each intermediate position preserves an escape route for the player around the box.
When pushing along a boundary (near walls), prefer moves that keep a parallel walking lane open; do not align boxes flush against walls in a way that removes the only bypass around them.
Do not push a box into any non-goal corner or 2-wall pocket; extend this to 'corridor dead-ends' where the box cannot be pulled out and the player cannot get behind it for reversal.

Prefer solving/clearing boxes that currently gate access to large free-space regions before moving other boxes; otherwise later pushes may require standing positions inside regions you have already sealed off.
If a push uses a standing cell that is part of a narrow passage, ensure that passage will remain traversable after the push (i.e., the box’s new position does not occupy or block that passage).

For any candidate push, also verify that the player can still reach at least one 'parking' region after the push (a region with enough space to maneuver around boxes); avoid pushes that trap the player in a small compartment.

When multiple boxes exist in the same corridor/row/column, avoid pushing one box behind another unless there is confirmed space to reorder them later; otherwise you may create an unreachable standing requirement between them.

Introduce a 'no-regret' rule: do not push a box away from a goal cell (or out of a goal corridor) unless the planner can certify a later sequence that restores access to push it back onto goals without requiring unreachable standing cells.
